subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: LiDAR: Peeling Back the Jungle
description: A short lesson to help you apply LiDAR: Peeling Back the Jungle.

hook.text: A laser technology that can see through dense forest canopy is rewriting the history of entire civilizations.

buildup.text: LiDAR fires millions of laser pulses from aircraft. Some pass through leaves and bounce off the ground below.

discovery.text: In Cambodia, LiDAR revealed that Angkor was the largest pre-industrial city on Earth — far bigger than maps showed.

twist.text: In Guatemala, it found 60,000 Maya structures, roads, and farms that no one had seen despite decades of ground surveys.

climax.text: LiDAR is finding so many sites so fast that there are not enough archaeologists to investigate them all.

punchline.text: We spent centuries searching jungles on foot. Lasers did more in a week.

quiz.question: What did LiDAR reveal about the Maya civilization in Guatemala?
options: The Maya had no roads or infrastructure between cities
60,000 structures, roads, and farms invisible from ground surveys
Maya cities were much smaller than previously estimated

details.summary: LiDAR technology fires laser pulses through forest canopy to map the ground surface below, revealing archaeological sites invisible from the ground or air. It has transformed tropical archaeology, discovering vast hidden cities and infrastructure networks beneath jungles worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Before LiDAR, tropical forests were archaeological blind spots. Ground survey is painfully slow, and traditional aerial photography cannot see through canopy.
takeaways: Laser pulses penetrate forest canopy to map ground surfaces
Has revealed hidden cities in Guatemala, Cambodia, and the Amazon
Transformed tropical archaeology by removing the canopy barrier

faq.question: What major discoveries has LiDAR made in tropical archaeology?
faq.answer: LiDAR revealed that Angkor in Cambodia covered over 1,000 square kilometers. In Guatemala, it found over 60,000 Maya structures. In the Amazon, it showed pre-Columbian earthworks across supposedly pristine forest. In Honduras, it found a rumored lost city in the Mosquitia jungle.

faq.question: How expensive is archaeological LiDAR survey?
faq.answer: Costs have dropped dramatically. Early surveys cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. Modern drone-based LiDAR systems can survey smaller areas affordably. The cost-benefit ratio is extraordinary — a single flight can discover more sites than decades of ground survey.
